traits.leaf_base_shape.note: Lucid family key, Melastomataceae (read 2026-10-17): base usually cuneate, rarely attenuate.

traits.leaf_incision.note: DELTA, Melastomataceae (read 2026-10-17): leaves simple, no lobing described; Lucid key (read 2026-10-17): no lobing.

traits.leaf_margin.note: DELTA, Melastomataceae (read 2026-10-17): margins entire or serrate; Lucid family key (read 2026-10-17): entire. Toothed (often finely) blades occur in a minority of species.

traits.leaf_shape.note: Lucid family key, Melastomataceae (read 2026-10-17): leaves usually broad-elliptic; full range linear to ovate, lanceolate, elliptic, obovate, orbicular. DELTA (read 2026-10-17): lanceolate, oblong or ovate. Miconia (nearly 1,900 species, Wikipedia (read 2026-10-17)) dominates.

traits.flower_merosity.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 345, 347: 4 to 5 sepals and petals, rarely 3 to 10.

traits.stamens.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 345, 347: stamens usually 8 or 10 in two whorls, often of two forms (formula 4+4 or 5+5).

traits.carpels.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 345, 347: carpels 3 to 5, rarely 2 to 15.

traits.corolla_shape.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 345: corolla of 4 to 5 free convolute petals. Free petals: rotate by PlantGen's free-petal rule; the book names no other corolla form.

traits.note: Hutchinson (vol. 1, 2nd ed., 1959), family 168 Melastomataceae: herbs, shrubs or trees; leaves simple, opposite or whorled, mostly with 3 to 9 veins running lengthwise from the base (read as palmate venation), rarely pinnately veined; no stipules; flowers regular, mostly showy; calyx a tube, free of the ovary or joined to it; petals free; stamens as many as to twice the petals, the anthers opening by a pore; ovary mostly inferior; fruit a capsule or a berry. The calyx tube is read as a hypanthium.

traits.inflorescence.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 345, 346, 347, family Melastomataceae: inflorescence cyme; read as "cyme".

traits.stem_cross_section.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 345, 346, 347, family Melastomataceae: stems 4-angled; read as {"square": "often"}.
